key_insight: Finite element simulations indicate that thermally stressed NiTi-based bilayer hinges can drive prescribed origami folding while reducing unit-cell dimensions by approximately 50% relative to previously reported designs.
engineering_relevance: Compact, self-folding structures could support minimally invasive delivery and controlled deployment of neurovascular implants.
method: Model thermal-mismatch bending in thin-film NiTi–molybdenum and NiTi–SS316L composites.
Optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape using finite element simulations.
Integrate hinges into a waterbomb origami unit cell to assess coordinated folding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based hinge optimization and coordinated folding in a complete waterbomb unit cell, but no experimental validation.
watch_item: Microscale fabrication tolerances and safe thermal actuation in vivo remain implementation concerns not validated in the abstract.
paper_title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
